subject: Re: Shaping Horizon Health pilot — packaging, quant & KV caching scope
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@horizonhealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot questions: packaging and quantization tradeoffs

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week — it was helpful. We're getting pressure from procurement to lock down the commercial shape of the pilot before our architecture review next Friday. Two quick asks from my side:

1) Can you send a compact matrix showing expected token-cost delta for the three configurations we discussed (base FP16, 4-bit quant, 3-bit quant + KV cache)? I need order-of-magnitude numbers to put in the MA plan.

2) On packaging: would Redwood allow a split pilot with a fixed monthly reserved block (dedicated) for peak hours and hosted call-through for burst? If so, what does that do to the unit price and the ability to apply optimizer credits we talked about?

Appreciate concise numbers and any implementation caveats — Derek from infra is cc'd and will look at technical constraints.

Best,

Maria Lopez
Senior Procurement Manager
Horizon Health

Attachments: horizon_requirements_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Derek Shaw <derek.shaw@horizonhealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 11:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot questions: packaging and quantization tradeoffs

Hi Maria — thanks, happy to clarify.

Short answers up front:
- We'll attach a one-page cost delta matrix (see attached redwood_pricing_grid_v3.pdf) with conservative per-token estimates for FP16, 4-bit, and 3-bit+KV cache. These are modeled on a 90-day pilot profile you shared.
- We support hybrid packaging: reserved "Dedicated" capacity for predictable throughput + hosted overflow. From an econ standpoint that lets us apply a pilot credit to the reserved commit and provide discounted hosted rates for overflow rather than full list pricing.

Key implementation caveats:
- 3-bit quant provides larger cost reductions but requires a short onboarding window to verify quality regressions on your prompt set — we'll reserve 2 engineer-days of QC in the pilot SOW.
- KV cache yields big per-token savings for conversational flows with long prefixes; savings scale with prefix hit-rate.
- Reserved blocks reduce per-token unit price but are time-bound; credits apply to committed spend only unless we explicitly extend a promo to overflow calls (we can do that for the pilot but need signoff).

I'll loop David from pricing to provide the numeric delta table and a draft MA shape for procurement to review.

Next step: I'll send the numeric sheet by EOD today and a short MA sketch tomorrow.

Thanks — Laura

-- 
Laura Bennett
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: FWD: Pilot questions: packaging and quantization tradeoffs

Team — forwarding Horizon's procurement note. Need a quick table and two commercial options:

Option A (Conservative): 90-day pilot, 2 GPU Dedicated reserved blocks (p99 throughput), apply 25% pilot credit to committed spend, overflow at hosted list - 10%.
Option B (Aggressive): 90-day pilot, 1 GPU Dedicated reserved + hosted overflow, apply 35% pilot credit to committed spend and extend a temporary 15% discount on overflow for the pilot period. Include 2 eng-days QC for 3-bit quant and an ops SLA of 99.5% for reserved capacity.

Questions for pricing:
- What are the per-token numbers for FP16 / 4-bit / 3-bit+KV cache on our recommended instance? Use the same model family as demo (rw-xl-2).
- Can we map the pilot credit as a prepaid credit (helps procurement signoff) or does it have to be a post-facto rebate?

Can you turn this into a short spreadsheet and a procurement-ready MA draft? Horizon is asking for numbers today.

Thanks — Laura

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Pilot questions: packaging and quantization tradeoffs

Laura / Vanessa,

Attached is the cost delta workbook (horizon_mam_estimates.xlsx) and a 1-page MA sketch. Highlights below:

- Per-token delta (rough guide, rounded):
  • FP16 (rw-xl-2): $0.00120 / token
  • 4-bit quant: $0.00078 / token (≈35% reduction)
  • 3-bit + KV cache (assume 60% cache hit on prefixes): effective $0.00042 / token (≈65% reduction vs FP16)

- Commercial mapping:
  Option A (Conservative): 25% pilot credit applied as a prepaid credit to the reserved commit; overflow billed at list -10%.
  Option B (Aggressive): 35% prepaid credit to commit; overflow discounted 15% for pilot; includes 2 eng-days QC and 99.5% reserved SLA. We can cap total prepaid credit to $50k for the pilot.

Notes/risks:
- 3-bit quant requires a failback path to 4-bit or FP16 if QA indicates unacceptable regressions; that impacts orchestration but not the pricing math.
- If Horizon wants the overflow discount to convert to post-pilot committed pricing, we need a minimum 6‑month commit in the follow-on.

I've placed the MA sketch in the Drive link below and attached the workbook. LMK if Horizon wants a DocuSign-ready SOW — I can turn it around tomorrow.

Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/s/hzn/horizon-hub-ss

David
